decision: Candaba is a high-priority wetland lead with historical fish-inventory sources, but the reviewed sources disagree in scope and counts and do not support a current, complete, rights-cleared species checklist. Preserve author-reported names as candidates and keep them out of public assertions.

waterbody.name: Candaba Swamp / Candaba Wetlands
scopeLimits: The 2020 inventory names Barangays San Agustin and Dukma Paralaya; this does not validate the full wetland extent.
The historical thesis and journal abstracts name Candaba Swamp or wetland but do not provide a validated waterbody polygon, sampling stations, or a complete municipality-to-wetland crosswalk.
No legal access, fishing boundary, salinity classification, or hydrological geometry was verified.

sources.title: Fish inventory and fishing practices in Candaba swamp, Philippines: their implication to fishermen’s income
sourceReportedScope: Barangays San Agustin and Dukma Paralaya
sources.access: Publisher PDF is linked directly; parsed/cached article text was reviewed. A fresh direct fetch timed out during this pass, so no local publisher PDF or cryptographic input hash is claimed.
sources.sourceReportedMethod: The article describes a descriptive inventory based on fish caught by local fishers and says identifications were morphology-based with expert validation. Its reviewed text does not provide voucher/catalog identifiers or a date-resolved sampling frame that can be independently checked here.
qualityIssues: The abstract says 14 species across 14 families, while a body passage describes five Cyprinidae plus ten other species, which sums to 15.
Several scientific-name strings are concatenated or have likely spelling/format issues in the published text. They are preserved verbatim and must not be silently normalized.
The conclusion maps the common name Hito to Hypostomus plecostomus; this common-name/taxon mapping requires independent voucher-level review.
The article's site labels do not establish the whole Candaba wetland, a current occurrence, abundance, catchability, or a complete local checklist.
sources.reuse: The publisher's item-level license statement was not independently verified in this pass. Do not reproduce its prose, tables, or figures; re-check the publisher license before any data reuse.
sources.disposition: Historical, author-reported candidate strings only. No accepted taxonomy, species assertion, diet claim, geometry, or app projection is created from this source.

sources.title: Species composition and length-weight relationship of fishes in the Candaba wetland on Luzon Island, Philippines

sources.reuse: No item-specific open license or table-reuse permission was verified. Do not reproduce the full species table from secondary sources.
sources.disposition: Independent historical aggregate lead, not a current inventory. Keep its reported richness separate from the 2020 paper; do not infer or copy species identities from the abstract.

sources.access: Official metadata and indexed abstract only; the PDF endpoint returned HTTP 404 in the prior review. No Candaba-specific table rows were available.

crossSourceReconciliation.2020CountConflict: Abstract reports 14 species, while a body count of five plus ten implies 15.
crossSourceReconciliation.reason: The sources differ by sampling years, site wording, scope, methods, accessible taxonomic detail, and completeness. Aggregate totals are not summed or merged into one present-day inventory.

nextStep: Continue Central Luzon source reconciliation with Angat reservoir/river and Pampanga River reaches including the Minalin Channel study. Keep wetland, river, brackish and coastal scope distinct, and use corrected taxon keys only for bounded occurrence searches; regional coverage remains incomplete.
